measured.fixture: fixtures/main.json: a synthetic filing with 6 tables on 6 pages, 6 lines, 2 periods, 5 units, 12 quotes, 6 questions, 18 planted answers
measured.authored_note: The filing, its numbers and the three planted answers per question were written for this experiment. The counts show how the two tests behave on these plants; they are not an error rate of any model.

on_unmeasured.why: Reported in the paper's abstract; not reproduced, and not comparable with the planted counts above.

claims.what: a benchmark of 1,000 questions over 90 recent 10-K and 10-Q filings from 45 US companies, with answer keys taken from the filers' inline XBRL tags
ten open instruct models of 7B to 21B parameters, each run on one consumer GPU, in three setups: plain, check then retry, and the model's own reasoning mode
accuracy with machine-checkable evidence spans 17.1% to 82.7% in the plain setup, and the best result is 84.5% for one 9B model
between 16 and 167 answers per 1,000 carry a wrong value for an answerable question yet pass every automatic check
in the plain setup, 57% of those check-passing wrong answers are scale or unit errors and 30% take another period or column of the right line
the reasoning mode significantly reduces such errors for 4 of the 5 models that offer it
retrying after a failed check raises accuracy by up to 3.9 points but never reduces the check-passing wrong answers
the upstream repository's tests, protocol and stored runs (described in its README, not executed here)
